newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL -- Xerox in freefall.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL -- Xerox in freefall.

text.p: Shares in Xerox Corp fell sharply preceding Friday's market open as investors bolted upon learning of the company's diappointing third quarter earnings.
Preceding the market open, Xerox shares fell seven points to 50, a slide traders said was hastened by Merrill Lynch's downgraded of the stock to near-term neutral from accumulate.
Xerox said it earned $0.68 per share in the third quarter, below the First Call consensus analyst estimate of $0.82.
In subsequent pre-open activity, traders said Xerox continued to decline, hitting 49-1/2.
Also, Silicon Graphics Inc fell to 20-7/8 from 21-1/2 after reporting a fiscal first quarter loss of $0.13 per share after a charge versus a profit of $0.33 per share.
Traders said Merrill's downgrade of Silicon Graphics to near-term neutral from accumulate and to long-term accumulate from buy also sapped the stock of support.
Iomega Corp shares rose to 25 from 22-7/8 on earnings strength and the company's intention to move to the New York Stock Exchange from Nasdaq, traders said.
Last night, Iomega said it earned $0.09 in the third quarter verusus $0.02, while revenues soared to $310.1 million from $84.7 million.
The company also said it will file an application to trade its securities on the NYSE, a move traders said tends to be bullish for a stock.
